content: There are various types of typology in languages. For example, in English the typology order is subject-verb-object (SVO) order, but in Japanese and Korean the order is subject-object-verb (SOV). We construct a typology-manipulated dataset to examine if the typology order of the training data influences the transfer learning results. If the model only learns the semantic mapping between different languages, changing English typology order from SVO to SOV should improve the transfer ability from English to Japanese. The method used to generate datasets is the same as BIBREF21.
